tests.title: The loader reads the sandbox section from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml, or ./config.toml when the variable is unset or empty, keeping profile file order
given: a temp dir A with config.toml holding [sandbox] provider="podman" and profiles "zeta" then "alpha"
a temp dir B with a different config.toml in the working directory
tests.when: ConfigPath and LoadConfig are called with XDG_CONFIG_HOME=A, then with it unset, then with it set to the empty string
then: with XDG set the path is A/config.toml and both profiles load in the order zeta, alpha
with XDG unset or empty the path is ./config.toml and B's content is loaded
tests.pseudocode: t.Setenv('XDG_CONFIG_HOME',A); cfg=LoadConfig(ConfigPath()); assert names(cfg)==['zeta','alpha']; unset; chdir(B); assert ConfigPath()=='./config.toml'

tests.title: A missing file or a file without [sandbox] yields a nil config, nil error and one info log line
given: one case with no config file and one case with a config.toml holding only [server]
a captured slog handler
tests.when: LoadConfig is called for each case and the start-up helper logs the disabled state
then: both calls return a nil config and a nil error
exactly one info record is logged and it says sandboxes are disabled
tests.pseudocode: cfg,err=LoadConfig(p); assert cfg==nil && err==nil; assert count(infoRecords)==1 && contains(msg,'disabled')

tests.title: For any string value in the sandbox section, ${NAME} is replaced and bare $ is untouched
given: environment variables with random names and values set via t.Setenv, and some left unset
tests.when: for any string composed of literal text, bare $ characters and ${NAME} references (to set or unset variables), placed in image, a secrets entry, a network_modes entry and an env value
then: every ${NAME} is replaced by the variable's value, or by an empty string when unset
every $ not followed by {NAME} is preserved
the same expansion applies in scalar, list and env-map values
tests.pseudocode: for s in gen_strings(): cfg=load(toml(s)); assert cfg.image==model_expand(s) for all four positions

tests.title: Expansion is limited to the sandbox section and uses literal $ handling
given: a config.toml where [server] and [workspace] values contain ${HOME_X} and where a sandbox env value contains a quote character and ${SANDBOX_TOKEN}
tests.when: the file is loaded with SANDBOX_TOKEN=abc and HOME_X set
then: the sandbox env value contains abc and the quote and still decodes
a value 'cost$5' stays 'cost$5'
values outside the sandbox section are not read or altered by the loader

tests.title: An unknown key under [sandbox] or a profile refuses with its full key path
given: a config with two profiles where profiles[1] has memroy_mb = 512
a second config with an unknown key sandbox.listenx
then: the error is non-nil and contains sandbox.profiles[1].memroy_mb
the second error contains sandbox.listenx

tests.title: Keys of apikit-owned sections never produce an unknown-key error
given: a config.toml with a valid [sandbox] plus [server], [database], [workspace] and OAuth tables containing keys the sandbox package does not know
then: the error is nil
the config decodes normally

tests.title: An unreadable or undecodable config file returns a wrapped error
given: one path to a file with mode 0000 (or a directory named config.toml) and one file with invalid TOML syntax
then: each returns a non-nil error
the error wraps the underlying read error, or a toml decode error respectively (errors.As / errors.Unwrap)

tests.title: With an invalid sandbox section af-hub still completes admin-token bootstrap, and otherwise exits before any listener opens
given: the af-hub binary built from cmd/af-hub
a temp XDG_CONFIG_HOME whose config.toml has an invalid [sandbox] section
a temp database and workspace path, and a free port
tests.when: af-hub is run once with --admin-email and once without it
then: the --admin-email run writes the admin token and exits 0
the run without it exits non-zero with the sandbox error on stderr
no TCP connection to the port succeeds and no queue worker log line appears in the second run
tests.pseudocode: run(bin,'--admin-email','a@b.c'); assert exit==0 && tokenFile exists; r=run(bin); assert r.exit!=0; assert !dial(port)

tests.title: A [sandbox] table with no provider fails naming sandbox.provider
given: a config with [sandbox] containing one valid profile but no provider, and one with provider = ""
then: the error contains sandbox.provider and says it is required

tests.title: provider gateway is unsupported and any other unknown provider lists accepted values
given: configs with provider="gateway" and provider="kubernetes"
then: the gateway error contains sandbox.provider and 'not supported by this build'
the other error contains sandbox.provider and podman
tests.pseudocode: assert contains(Validate(gw),'not supported by this build'); assert contains(Validate(k8s),'podman')

tests.title: Engine options default and are passed to the provider constructor unchanged
given: a recording provider factory standing in for podman.New
one config with engine_binary="docker", runtime="runsc", userns="keep-id" and one config omitting all three
tests.when: the provider is built from each config
then: the first receives Binary docker, Runtime runsc, UserNS keep-id
the second receives Binary podman, Runtime empty, UserNS empty

tests.title: max_ttl rejects invalid or non-positive values and defaults to 4h
given: configs with max_ttl = "soon", "0s", "-1h" and one with max_ttl absent and a profile ttl of 4h
then: the invalid values produce an error containing sandbox.max_ttl
the absent value passes with an effective max_ttl of 4h

tests.title: network_modes rejects empty and duplicate entries and defaults to [none]
given: configs with network_modes ["none",""], ["none","bridge","none"] and one absent
then: the bad lists produce an error containing sandbox.network_modes and the offending index
the absent key yields an effective ["none"]

tests.title: A sandbox section with no profiles fails
given: a config with provider podman and no [[sandbox.profiles]]
then: the error contains sandbox.profiles and says at least one profile is required

tests.title: Missing, malformed and duplicate profile names are reported with the profile identifier
given: profiles with names: missing (index 0), "Upper", "-lead", a 64-character name, and two profiles named "dev"
then: the missing name is reported as sandbox.profiles[0] with the field name
each malformed name error names the profile and name
the duplicate is reported naming dev and name
a 63-character valid name and 'a_b-c1' pass

tests.title: Two default profiles fail, one or none pass
given: three configs: two profiles with default=true, one with default=true, none with default
then: the first error contains default and both profile names
the other two return no error

tests.title: A missing or empty image is reported with profile and field
given: profile "a" without image and profile "b" with image = ""
then: the error contains a and image, and b and image

tests.title: Negative or fractional resource values fail, zero passes
given: profiles with cpus=-1, memory_mb=-5, pids=1.5, disk_mb=-1 and a profile with all four set to 0
then: each bad field is reported with the profile name and the field name
the all-zero profile produces no error
tests.pseudocode: for f in [cpus,memory_mb,pids,disk_mb]: assert contains(err, profile+' '+f)

tests.title: A profile network outside network_modes fails; an absent network defaults to none
given: network_modes ["none"] with a profile network="bridge"
a profile with no network key
then: the first error contains the profile name, network and bridge
the second passes and the validated network is none

tests.title: ttl is required, positive, parseable and at most max_ttl
given: max_ttl="1h" and profiles with ttl missing, "abc", "0s", "61m", and "1h"
then: the first four each produce an error naming the profile and ttl
ttl "1h" equal to max_ttl passes

tests.title: require_landlock defaults to false when omitted
given: a valid profile without require_landlock and one with require_landlock=true
then: the first validated profile has RequireLandlock false
the second has true

tests.title: Invalid secret names are reported with profile, list and index
given: a profile with secrets ["OK","1BAD"] and optional_secrets ["has-dash"]
then: the error names the profile and secrets[1]
the error names the profile and optional_secrets[0]

tests.title: Case-insensitive duplicate secret names fail within and across lists
given: profile with secrets ["API_KEY","api_key"]
profile with secrets ["TOKEN"] and optional_secrets ["token"]
then: each error names the profile and the repeated name

tests.title: Reserved names such as GIT_PAT are accepted as secrets
given: a profile with secrets ["GIT_PAT"] and optional_secrets ["GH_TOKEN"]
then: no error is returned

tests.title: An invalid env key is reported by key without its value
given: a profile with env {"BAD-KEY":"supersecretvalue"}
then: the error contains the profile, env and BAD-KEY
the error does not contain supersecretvalue

tests.title: An env key colliding with a secret name ignoring case fails without leaking the value
given: a profile with secrets ["GIT_PAT"] and env {"git_pat":"leakme"}, and another with optional_secrets ["X"] and env {"x":"leakme"}
then: each error names the profile and the colliding key
no error contains leakme

tests.title: For any section with N independent static faults, one joined error contains all N messages
given: a catalogue of independent fault injectors (bad max_ttl, bad network_modes, bad name, duplicate name, missing image, negative resource, bad ttl, bad secret, env collision)
tests.when: for any non-empty subset of fault injectors applied to distinct profiles or deployment keys of an otherwise valid section
then: Validate returns exactly one error value
its text contains the failure message of each injected fault
tests.pseudocode: for subset in gen_subsets(): err=Validate(apply(subset)); for f in subset: assert contains(err,f.expected)

tests.title: After static validation the provider is built and List is called once with a deadline within 10 seconds
given: a valid config and a test-double provider that records List contexts and advertises network mode none
then: the double records exactly one List call
the context had a deadline no more than 10 seconds in the future when called
tests.pseudocode: New(cfg,fake); assert fake.listCalls==1; assert fake.deadline - callTime <= 10s

tests.title: Static failures are reported without building the provider or probing
given: a config with a duplicate profile name and a recording provider factory and double
tests.when: the service is started from that config
then: the returned error names the duplicate
the factory is not invoked and List has zero calls

tests.title: Provider construction failure, List error and List timeout refuse start with the sandbox: prefix
given: a factory returning an error, a double whose List returns 'engine down', and a double whose List blocks until its context is done
tests.when: the service is started with each
then: every error starts with "sandbox:" and contains sandbox.provider and sandbox.engine_binary
the first two contain the provider error text
the blocking case returns within about 10 seconds with a deadline error

tests.title: A network_modes entry the provider does not support refuses start
given: network_modes ["none","host"] and a double whose capabilities list only none
then: the error contains sandbox.network_modes and host

tests.title: Each profile is converted to a Spec with image, fixed env only, network, resources, TTL and landlock and checked once
given: two profiles with secrets ["GIT_PAT"], optional_secrets ["X"] and env {"LANG":"C"}, a double recording the Spec seen by CheckSpec (or the real CheckSpec against double capabilities)
then: CheckSpec is run once per profile
Spec.Image, Network, Resources, TTL (equal to ttl) and RequireLandlock equal the profile values
Spec.Env equals {LANG: C} and contains no secret names

tests.title: A profile refused by CheckSpec fails start naming the profile and the error text
given: a double whose capabilities reject profile "big" (for example require_landlock unsupported) and accept profile "small"
then: the error names big and includes the CheckSpec error text
small is not reported

tests.title: A fractional cpus value refuses start when AgentKit's CPU field is a whole number
given: a profile with cpus = 1.5 and a valid double provider
AgentKit's CPU field type checked at implementation time; if it is a float the case is skipped and 1.5 passes
then: with an integer CPU field the error contains the profile name and cpus
a whole value such as cpus = 2 is accepted

tests.title: The service keeps provider and profiles and never calls Create or Destroy
given: a recording double provider and a valid config
tests.when: New is called and the service's accessors are used
then: the service exposes the provider and the validated profiles
the double records zero Create and zero Destroy calls
tests.pseudocode: svc=New(cfg,fake); assert svc.Provider()==fake && len(svc.Profiles())==2; assert fake.create==0 && fake.destroy==0

tests.title: Permissions returns exactly sandboxes:read and sandboxes:write
then: the result equals [{sandboxes read} {sandboxes write}] in that order

tests.title: For any PAT, read access holds exactly when it has sandboxes:read or sandboxes:write
tests.when: for any permission list drawn from sandboxes:read, sandboxes:write and unrelated scopes, on a PAT credential
then: canReadSandboxes is true iff the list contains sandboxes:read or sandboxes:write
tests.pseudocode: for perms in gen(): assert canRead(pat(perms)) == ('sandboxes:read' in perms or 'sandboxes:write' in perms)

tests.title: Any api_key or admin_token credential gets read access regardless of permissions
tests.when: for any permissions list (including empty) on an api_key or admin_token credential
then: canReadSandboxes is true
tests.pseudocode: for t in [api_key,admin_token]: for perms in gen(): assert canRead({t,perms})

tests.title: No credential gets 401 before the feature-off check
given: the route registered once with a nil service (disabled) and once with a service, no auth middleware setting AuthInfo
tests.when: GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles is sent in each setup
then: both return 401 in apikit's error envelope
neither returns the sandboxes_disabled error

tests.title: With the feature off every authenticated caller gets 404 sandboxes_disabled
given: routes registered with a nil service
callers: admin_token, api_key, and a PAT with no sandbox scopes
tests.when: GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles is sent as each caller
then: each response is 404
the body is exactly {"error":{"code":404,"message":"sandboxes are not enabled on this hub","error_type":"sandboxes_disabled"}}

tests.title: With the feature on a PAT without sandbox scopes gets 403
given: routes registered with a valid service
a PAT holding only secrets:list
then: the status is 403 in apikit's error envelope
a PAT with sandboxes:read gets 200 and one with sandboxes:write gets 200

tests.title: The listing returns every profile sorted by name with the documented fields
given: a service with profiles "zeta" (ttl 90m, default, cpus 1, memory_mb 512, pids 100, disk_mb 0) and "alpha"
an admin_token caller
then: the status is 200 and the body is {"profiles":[alpha, zeta]}
each element has name, default, image, network, ttl_seconds, resources {cpus, memory_mb, pids, disk_mb}, secrets, optional_secrets, env_keys and require_landlock
zeta's ttl_seconds is the JSON integer 5400
tests.pseudocode: assert names==['alpha','zeta']; assert p.ttl_seconds==5400; assert keys(p)==expected

tests.title: For any profile the three name lists are sorted ascending JSON arrays, never null
tests.when: for any profile whose secrets, optional_secrets and env keys are random valid names in any order, including empty lists
then: each of secrets, optional_secrets and env_keys is a JSON array
each array is sorted in ascending order
an empty list renders as [] and not null
tests.pseudocode: for p in gen(): body=get(); for f in lists: assert isArray(body[f]) && body[f]==sorted(body[f])

tests.title: The listing makes no provider call and no database read and still answers after the engine fails
given: a service built with a double that counts every method call after start
the handler wired without any database handle
the double afterwards set to fail all calls
then: the status is 200 with the full profile list
the double records zero calls during the request
tests.pseudocode: fake.failAll(); fake.reset(); rec=get(); assert rec.Code==200 && fake.total()==0

tests.title: Every authorised caller receives an identical profile list
given: a service with a fixed set of profiles
tests.when: for any authorised caller (admin_token, api_key, PAT with read or write scope) with any user ID, key ID and workspace memberships
then: the response body bytes are identical for all callers
tests.pseudocode: base=get(admin).Body; for c in gen_callers(): assert get(c).Body==base

tests.title: For any sandbox section no env value appears in the listing, logs or errors
given: a captured slog handler and a unique random sentinel as each env value
tests.when: for any sandbox section with random env values, valid or containing static faults, loaded, validated, started with a double and listed
then: no env value is a substring of the listing body
no env value is a substring of any log record
no env value is a substring of any returned error
tests.pseudocode: for cfg in gen(): err,logs,body=run(cfg); for v in envValues(cfg): assert v not in err+logs+body

tests.title: Enabling the feature logs one info line with only provider and profile names
given: a captured slog handler, a valid config whose image, secrets and env values are distinctive strings
tests.when: the start-up helper logs the enabled state
then: exactly one info record is emitted
its attributes are only the provider name and the list of profile names
no image, secret, env or max_ttl value appears in the record

tests.title: Listing omits provider, options and max_ttl and construction needs no store or database
given: a config with provider podman, engine_binary "/opt/podman-x", runtime "runsc", max_ttl "3h"
tests.when: the service is built and the listing is requested
then: the body contains none of podman-x, runsc, 'podman', max_ttl or 3h
the exported constructors and loaders compile without a *secrets.Store or *sql.DB parameter
tests.pseudocode: assert !contains(body,'runsc') && !contains(body,'max_ttl'); New(cfg, provider) compiles with no db

tests.title: afc sandbox profiles prints the response as one JSON document
given: an httptest hub answering GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles with a fixed profiles JSON body and recording the Authorization header
tests.when: runRootCmd is run with --endpoint-url, --api-key and sandbox profiles
then: stdout is one JSON document equal to the response body
the request carried the configured credential
the exit code is 0

tests.title: afc sandbox profiles rejects positional arguments without a request
given: an httptest hub counting requests
tests.when: runRootCmd is run with sandbox profiles extra
then: the command fails with a usage error
the exit code is non-zero
the hub saw zero requests

tests.title: Error statuses from the hub are reported through CLIHandleError with nothing on stdout
given: an httptest hub answering 404 with error_type sandboxes_disabled, then 401, then 403 in apikit's envelope
tests.when: runRootCmd runs sandbox profiles against each
then: stdout is empty
the error message mentions the hub's message
the exit code equals apikit's mapping for each status and is non-zero
tests.pseudocode: for s in [404,401,403]: out,err=run(...); assert out=='' && ExitCode(err)==apikitCode(s)

tests.title: BuildRootCommand registers the sandbox group whose only subcommand is profiles
tests.when: BuildRootCommand() is built and the sandbox command is looked up
then: a command named sandbox exists
its subcommands are exactly [profiles]

tests.title: Build files wire the agentkit-go sibling like apikit
given: go.mod, containers/hub/Containerfile, Makefile and the two workflow files read as text
then: go.mod has a require for the agentkit-go sandbox module and a replace to ../agentkit-go next to the apikit replace
the Containerfile copies from the agentkit build context
the build-hub-container target passes --build-context agentkit=../agentkit-go
inc-build-hub.yaml and build-hub-cli.yaml clone agentkit-go and inc-build-hub.yaml passes it as a build context

tests.title: afc and internal/cli do not depend on internal/sandboxes or agentkit-go
given: the repository module graph
tests.when: go list -deps is run for ./cmd/afc and ./internal/cli
then: neither list contains internal/sandboxes or any agentkit-go package

tests.title: A valid sandbox section starts the service and a PAT with sandboxes:read lists profiles
given: a temp XDG_CONFIG_HOME config.toml with provider podman and two profiles using ${NAME} env values and secret names
a test-double sandbox.Provider with network mode none that records calls
an echo server with a test auth middleware
tests.when: LoadConfig, validation and New run with the double, routes are registered and a PAT with sandboxes:read sends GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles
then: start succeeds with exactly one List call and one CheckSpec per profile
the start-up info log has provider and profile names only
the response is 200 sorted by name with secret names and env key names
no env value appears in the body
tests.pseudocode: cfg=LoadConfig(ConfigPath()); svc=New(cfg,fake); RegisterRoutes(api,svc); rec=get(pat(['sandboxes:read'])); assert 200 and sorted and no env values

tests.title: afc sandbox profiles prints the profiles served by the real handler
given: an httptest server hosting the real sandboxes route over a service built with a double provider
the real cli.BuildRootCommand, run from an internal/sandboxes test package
tests.when: the root command is executed with --endpoint-url, --api-key and sandbox profiles
then: the handler answers 200 from memory
stdout is one JSON document equal to the handler's body
the exit code is 0

tests.title: An invalid sandbox section refuses start with every failure and no provider contact
given: a config.toml with an unknown profile key, a duplicate profile name and a ttl over max_ttl
the af-hub binary with a fake engine_binary that records invocations to a file
tests.when: af-hub is started against that config
then: the process exits non-zero before any HTTP listener opens
stderr contains the unknown key path, the duplicate name with name, and the ttl field with the profile name
the engine binary was never invoked

tests.title: Without a [sandbox] section hub starts and the route answers 404 sandboxes_disabled
given: a config.toml with no [sandbox] table
the real start-up wiring with sandboxes.Permissions() appended and routes registered in disabled mode
tests.when: the server starts and an authenticated client sends GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles
then: one info line says sandboxes are disabled
the sandboxes:read and sandboxes:write scopes are registered
the response is 404 with error_type sandboxes_disabled and message 'sandboxes are not enabled on this hub'
tests.pseudocode: cfg=LoadConfig(p); assert cfg==nil; RegisterRoutes(api,nil); rec=get(admin); assert 404 and error_type=='sandboxes_disabled'
